header:
Date: 2025-04-22 | Time: 15:00-15:57 UTC | Duration: 57 mins
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Head DS, Nova), Lisa Gomez (CTO, Nova), Hannah Lee (Security), Mark Rivers (ML Eng)
summary: POC scoping call to align on success criteria, workload sizing and benchmarks; discussed commercial guardrails for the pilot (credits, caps, timeline and contracting path). Agreed to a 30-day pilot with recommended $7k credits pending final traffic profile and a benchmark run. Action items assigned for pricing, benchmark setup, and security docs.
topics: Success criteria: latency, throughput, quality metrics
Workload sizing: RPS, concurrency, token distribution
Benchmarks: synthetic vs production replay, cost per 1M tokens
Pilot commercial guardrails: credits, caps, scope, timebox
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're here to scope the POC and the commercial guardrails, Alex from Redwood, Priya from our SE team is with me.
[00:07] Samir Patel: Hi all, Samir here, we wanted to make sure the pilot covers our clinical QA flows and anonymized note extraction.
[00:13] Lisa Gomez: Hi this is Lisa, quick ask up front - we need to understand the path to procurement; our legal and procurement teams will need clear pilot terms.
[00:20] Priya Nair: Totally, we'll cover pilot terms, credits and also benchmarks. Quick intro question - what's your expected peak RPS and average tokens per request?
[00:29] Mark Rivers: Right now in staging we're seeing bursts up to 120 requests per minute, so about 2 RPS sustained, but peaks around 8 RPS. Typical payloads are 400-800 tokens for our note summarization.
[00:42] Samir Patel: Also for Q/A flows it's shorter, like 50-150 tokens. Our main success criteria are: 1) latency under 500ms p95 for short QA, 2) extraction F1 > 0.88 on our testset, and 3) cost per request below our internal threshold - we'll share numbers.
[00:59] Alex Chen: Great, latency goals sound reasonable; on hosted Redwood API for models in the 13B-range p95 for 150 tokens typically under 300-400ms depending on batching. For 400-800 tokens that will be higher, obviously.
[01:14] Priya Nair: For the POC we'll propose two tracks: Hosted quick pilot (fastest to run) and a Dedicated trial if you want reserved capacity. Hosted pilot is simpler for a 30-day timebox.
[01:25] Hannah Lee: From security perspective we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, audit logs, and KMS integration for keys. Also data residency - we need EU-only for certain subsets.
[01:36] Alex Chen: We can provide SOC2 reports, SAML SSO, and support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments. For hosted piloting we can restrict region and enable logging controls; we'll send a security packet.
[01:47] Lisa Gomez: On commercial guardrails, what do you typically do for credits and caps for pilots?
[01:52] Priya Nair: Common pattern: timeboxed 30-day pilot with a credit allocation that covers expected testing plus 20% buffer. For a workload like yours we usually recommend $5k-$10k in credits; based on the numbers Mark shared we think $7k is a good starting point.
[02:07] Samir Patel: How do caps work? We don't want surprises if someone fires a long batch job.
[02:12] Alex Chen: We can set hard caps at the project level and per-user API keys. Also rate limits and quota alerts. If you hit the cap the calls will be rejected; we can also set auto-notify thresholds at 50/75/90%.
[02:24] Mark Rivers: Cool. For benchmarking, we want to run a production-replay for 24 hours and also a synthetic 1k request run for latency numbers.
[02:33] Priya Nair: That works. We'll provide a benchmark harness (we have a repo) and a runbook. For the synthetic run we'll do 1k requests with your token distribution to measure p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1M tokens estimate.
[02:46] Samir Patel: What's typical cost reporting look like? We need token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards.
[02:52] Alex Chen: Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route and model. We can export CSVs for procurement.
[03:00] Lisa Gomez: Procurement path - our procurement will want an SOW or a short pilot agreement and a PO. How long does procurement usually take on your side?
[03:09] Alex Chen: For standard pilot agreements it's usually under 2 weeks internally. Procurement on the customer side varies - typically 2-6 weeks depending on legal review. We try to keep the pilot terms simple: timebox, credit cap, data handling, and a termination clause.
[03:22] Hannah Lee: On data handling - we need to confirm logs retention and whether we can opt out of telemetry.
[03:28] Priya Nair: You can opt out; for hosted pilots we can disable retention or set short retention windows and ensure PII is redacted on ingest as part of the runbook. We'll include that in the security packet.
[03:40] Mark Rivers: Benchmark detail - will you run on the same model we'll use in production? We want the test to reflect our production spec: a 13B quantized variant on A100 (or equivalent).
[03:51] Priya Nair: For hosted we select a model variant with comparable performance profile; for Dedicated we can spin up the exact runtime on similar GPU types. We'll document the exact model and quantization level used in the benchmark.
[04:03] Samir Patel: Success criteria recap: p95 latency thresholds, extraction F1, and cost per 1M tokens under $X - we'll put the exact cost threshold in the doc. Also timeline: 30-day pilot starting when contracts signed.
[04:16] Alex Chen: Right - proposed commercial guardrails: 30-day timebox, $7k credits by default, hard caps on usage, and a clear pilot SOW. Post-pilot options: convert credits into committed monthly dedicated capacity or transition to hosted billing.
[04:29] Lisa Gomez: If the pilot goes well and we want Dedicated, what's typical lead time for Dedicated capacity?
[04:34] Priya Nair: Depends on region and capacity, but typically 2-6 weeks to allocate and test Dedicated pools; enterprise track could be faster with committed terms.
[04:43] Samir Patel: For our internal signoff we'll need: benchmark report, security artifacts, and estimated run rate if we move to production.
[04:51] Alex Chen: We'll provide a benchmark report including p50/p95/p99, cost per 1M tokens, and recommended batching/quantization settings to meet your cost targets.
[04:59] Mark Rivers: Any typical blockers you've seen? Like model regressions during pilot due to prompt drift?
[05:05] Priya Nair: Yep prompt drift and data distribution shift are common. We'll set up a small eval harness so you can run your evals daily and set regression alerts. Also recommend snapshotting prompts and seed test sets.
[05:16] Hannah Lee: Contractually we may need an NDA in place before sharing production prompts.
[05:20] Alex Chen: We can move an NDA quickly; we'll also attach a minimal pilot SOW that doesn't expose sensitive prompt content.
[05:27] Samir Patel: On the benchmark specifics - can Redwood help with a tokenization mismatch? Our tokenizer is custom for clinical notes.
[05:34] Priya Nair: We can run your tokenizer locally as part of the harness; please share the tokenizer and we'll ensure the benchmark uses identical token counts.
[05:42] Alex Chen: OK let's put down explicit numbers for the benchmark: synthetic 1k requests with your token distribution, 24-hour production replay at your staging RPS, and a 1000-sample QA accuracy run.
[05:55] Lisa Gomez: For commercial guardrails I'd like a clause that says pilot credits won't be auto-converted to billing without explicit PO. Procurement hates surprise charges.
[06:03] Alex Chen: Absolutely - credits are applied only with written acceptance; we also set hard quota enforcement so there's no accidental overage.
[06:11] Samir Patel: If we need EU-only data handling mid-pilot, how fast can you switch the region?
[06:17] Priya Nair: For hosted we can spin a region-restricted project; it may require re-ingestion for some datasets but it can be done within a few days for the pilot. For Private deployments we'd provision in EU region per your VPC.
[06:28] Mark Rivers: Good. Who will be the primary contact for technical issues during the pilot?
[06:33] Alex Chen: Priya will be the SE on-call for bench runs, Alex as AE for commercial and procurement, and we'll loop in solutions engineering as needed.
[06:41] Priya Nair: We'll also provide a dedicated Slack channel for the pilot and set office hours.
[06:47] Samir Patel: What about success gating? If we miss the latency target but meet extraction F1, do we consider it a partial success?
[06:55] Alex Chen: We recommend defining pass/fail criteria per metric and a weighted scoring: e.g., F1 50%, latency 30%, cost 20%. We'll include a scoring sheet in the pilot SOW so everyone's aligned.
[07:07] Lisa Gomez: That's helpful. On procurement: after pilot acceptance, what's the path to convert credits to committed contract?
[07:13] Alex Chen: Typically a statement of work outlining committed throughput, a capacity price table, and either a monthly subscription or annual reserved capacity contract. We'll share a transition playbook that lists legal steps and expected timelines.
[07:24] Hannah Lee: Are there any data deletion guarantees at pilot end?
[07:28] Priya Nair: Yes we have post-pilot data deletion procedures; we can confirm retention windows and deletion certificate if required.
[07:35] Mark Rivers: OK let's get the benchmark on the calendar - our team can provide a staging dataset.
[07:41] Alex Chen: Great we'll propose Wednesday next week for the 2-hour benchmark run. Priya will share the runbook and repo link.
[07:47] Samir Patel: One more question - do you offer a temporary SLA for pilot availability?
[07:52] Alex Chen: For pilots we don't typically provide a formal SLA, but we commit operational support and escalation paths. For Dedicated we can include SLA terms in the reserved contract.
[08:02] Lisa Gomez: Alright let's recap next steps.
[08:05] Alex Chen: Recap - Redwood sends pricing spreadsheet and $7k credit recommendation, security packet and SOC2, Priya sends benchmark harness, Nova shares traffic profile and prompts, schedule benchmark next week, legal/Proc to review short pilot SOW.
[08:19] Samir Patel: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[08:21] Lisa Gomez: Thanks, talk soon.
[08:23] [call ends]

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-hears (e.g., "K V cash" instead of KV cache), filler words, and speaker overlaps. The transcript has been lightly cleaned but preserves conversational artifacts.
